answer.text: Stock prices fully reflect all past trading info (prices, volumes)

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the weak-form of the Efficient Markets Hypothesis, current stock prices already reflect all historical prices, returns, and trading-volume data. As a result, the workbook treats technical analysis — which is built on these past data series — as irrelevant for producing superior returns. The Trap: "Only insiders can outperform" describes a stronger form of efficiency (semi-strong/strong-form considerations). "Fundamental analysis always works" and "markets are always wrong" each contradict the weak-form statement directly. Note: The weak-form claim addresses past trading information specifically; it does not by itself rule out information advantages from fundamental or non-public information, which are addressed by the stronger forms of EMH.
